text:
sarah_sales: @james_dealdesk quick one — SageWorks (EU legal entity) wants a non-standard payment flow for a ~$420k ARR deal. They propose: 30% upfront, 40% upon POC acceptance (90d), 30% net60 after go-live. Also want a 10% holdback on the final payment until we hit agreed latency P95 < 350ms for 30 days. They asked for the invoice to be sent to their Ireland subsidiary (VAT handling) and for us to accept a PO with net60 on the final tranche. Can we get deal-desk + finance buy-in? :thinking_face:

james_dealdesk: thanks — a few flags. (1) layered schedules + holdback = revenue recognition headaches. (2) any holdback tied to SLOs needs concrete acceptance criteria and timebox. (3) discounts: they asked for 15% commit discount; is that on full ARR or only on committed portion?

omar_finance: cc @james_dealdesk — finance view: net60 on any tranche after go-live ok, but we need credit check and AR workflow. For VAT we must invoice the Irish entity and collect VAT reg #. Wire/ACH preferred for upfront/POs. Also need CFO sign-off for >$400k with nonstandard terms.

leila_ps: POC acceptance needs to be machine-checkable. Proposal: define 3 objective checks in SOW — (a) end-to-end inference at customer dataset with 95% pass on correctness suites, (b) latency P95 < 350ms on 10k sample queries, (c) integration tests pass in their staging. If all pass, the 40% POC tranche releases within 7 business days. We can add an 8-week rollback window for regression.

maria_cust: SageWorks product lead emailed: they need the staged payment because procurement can only approve 40% at POC. They're ok with the SLOs but want the holdback to be 60 days not 30. Willing to sign explicit SOW acceptance criteria.

james_dealdesk: proposed counter: (1) accept 30% upfront, (2) 40% at POC acceptance if SOW objective tests are met, (3) final 30% but move to net30 instead of net60 and drop the 10% holdback OR keep 30% net60 with 5% holdback. Want to reduce open AR exposure. Also discount calc: 15% applies to committed ARR only, not overages.

omar_finance: +1 to james. If legal approves the SOW language for holdback, finance can tolerate a 5% holdback for 60 days. Require PO scan + signed SOW before we ship. Document the billing entity clearly.

leila_ps: will draft SOW language for the acceptance tests and holdback clause. Quick snippet I propose to include in SOW:

```
POC acceptance criteria (sample):
- Correctness: >=95% on provided eval set
- Latency: median < 200ms, P95 < 350ms across 10k sample queries
- Integration: successful end-to-end runbook execution on staging
Upon automated verification, Customer issues written acceptance and invoice due as per schedule.
```

billing-bot: Invoice draft created (ID: INV-2026-0921) for 30% upfront. Attached: provisional schedule, billing entity = SageWorks Ireland Ltd.

james_dealdesk: conditional approve from deal desk: approve the modified schedule (30/40/30 with 5% holdback) subject to: legal approves SOW wording, finance completes credit check, and CFO signs off on exception. Also update discount terms to apply to committed ARR only.

omar_finance: I'll run the credit check now and route to CFO if green. Please attach customer's purchase order and VAT #.

sarah_sales: thanks all — i'll send the PO + VAT now, @leila_ps ping me the SOW draft when ready. Going to ledger the path: we prefer final net60 with 5% holdback but will accept net30 if CFO pushes back. Will post an update here once CFO responds. :white_check_mark:
